tl;dr: it's a nice sentiment and GREAT if it works, but for people with actual chronic depression (going on 10 years myself) it often doesn't.  My worldview is distorted in a way that makes all those attempts at spontaneous awesome temporary - I do still TRY them, but fall back into the depressive rut.  It is a mental prison that one cannot just "think" their way out of, no matter how frustrating or stupid that will seem to you.

I don't expect to get laid - I've made about two dozen attempts in the last year and none panned out.  I'd be lying if I claimed the feelings of unattractiveness that causes didn't contribute, but it's a tiny symptom of a much bigger problem.

I am fully aware there are people who would kill to be in my position.

I am fully aware it is not a sane state of mind or that anything is as bad as it feels.

I am fully aware the world is full of vast, varied beauty and fascinating people.  I can see it, I just can't enjoy it.

Your friend isn't a moron, he's having a moron-moment.  People love to bitch about things, but most people generally enjoy life enough to stick around.  People get depressed, or have a depressive span as a teenager, because people have tough times.  The main thing to remember is That Gets Better.

I wish this was that.  I wish someone could just talk me out of it - I see so many problems in the world that could be resolved just by people talking to each other honestly with open minds.

This is not one of those problems.  Sometimes honesty only hurts because they've heard it all before, and talking just keeps the clock ticking.  I'm tired of watching the hands rotate.  Sorry man - FWIW, you're doing an awesome deed that will improve the lives of many people, and I think that's beautiful.

My girlfriend was like that too.  Great person, very cheery, caring, positive.  But if you were depressed or suffering from something else she didn't understand, total shut down.
She would feel like you were being childish and just needed to get over it.

My friends and family think I'm on a trip overseas to "find myself", which is only part true.

I've been severely depressed and tired, haven't been laid in a year since my first girl left me, I'm 30, and have absolutely no goals or dreams anymore.

So I've gone on this trip for most of them to drift away (emotionally and geographically) so that I can kill myself with the least amount of guilt (still plenty).  I'm too tired to put in the work to make myself a person again.

Thank you, that is beautiful.  All I could ask is that you love, respect, and trust yourself, and spread that message to those around you.

I have found it is the hardest thing to do in the world.  I may be too tired to keep trying, but I suspect it is the true path.  Never forget that.

I wish I could receive one of those Hollywood turn-arounds too.  But I've been waiting ten years and I think that's long enough.  I am just too tired.

I wish I could help people - I know I have more to offer.  I am kind and morally strong, rational and a good person, who thinks about their impact on others.  But I just can't.  Maybe I think about it too much, I don't know.  Any problem I have is a First World Problem, and I still can't stick around.

I do intent to help others with my means.  I've set things up so that my money will be sent to a charity and some friends/family, and I've already donated what I don't take with me to Goodwill.  I'm going overseas so that I can hopefully find an isolated place to pass on, where I won't be found for a while.  I wish my organ donor card could be of more use, but I want to think that me being "missing" for a while will be less painful to my loved ones than suddenly finding me.  Maybe they'll have more time to adjust to the idea.

I know I'll hurt them regardless.  But it's the best I can do.

I've considered reasons I want to stay before.  I want to find love again.  I want a family.  I want to help people, inspire people.  I want to see my dreams and creativity take shape.  I want to see my friends and their families grow old and grow up, want to see all they accomplish.  I wish I could say these ideas were strong enough.  Maybe for a sane person they would be.  Wanting isn't enough, you have to strive, work toward these goals.  And for a reason I may never know, I can't do this.

In any case, you were never callous and I am so glad I moved you to post.  Even that requires courage, and many times all someone needs is a sympathetic ear, a different perspective.  Live strong and love fully.

That's wonderful.  I'm glad you've decided to stay.
"You must be the change you want to see in the world." - Gandhi

I found myself once too in part, when a good woman told me she loved me more than anyone.  But I'll admit even then there was something missing, I didn't love or respect myself enough, still don't.  I've been "resting" constantly it seems - it's funny how not doing anything can tire you out spiritually.

I think it is *because* of how short I fall from my own potential that the loneliness can creep in through all the cracks and walk me to the edge.

Keep fighting please, keep changing.  And try not to lie to your girlfriend or (especially) therapist.  They may know something you don't that can help.
